platforms.name: Linux bash
platforms.notes: v1.2.0 (2026-08-17): added before_implement/after_implement extension-hook dispatch to the execute command and both per-agent SKILL peers (instruction-only, no new script), with a skip-own-guard rule for hooks whose extension is speckit-superpowers-bridge; new tests/test-implement-hooks-dispatch.sh brings the suite to 7/7 green. Prior 0.11.1 re-verification (2026-06-18) remains valid: local specify CLI upgraded from the official github/spec-kit v0.11.1 tag; workflow step catalog support and shell-step output_format: json are upstream workflow-engine capabilities requiring no bridge adoption. Superpowers 6.0.0 evidence from 2026-06-17 remains valid: every Superpowers skill name the bridge invokes is unchanged in 6.0.0.

platforms.name: Windows PowerShell
platforms.notes: Native Windows PowerShell 5.1 evidence from v1.0.0 (2026-06-04) retained: the ps script flavor is byte-identical in v1.2.0 (the v1.2.0 change is instruction-only in execute.md + SKILL.md; no .ps1/.sh script changed), so prior validation remains the truthful evidence row. Windows Spec Kit CLI 0.8.10 required PYTHONUTF8=1 for clean Unicode install output.

The Superpowers 6.0.0 surface audit + smoke suite for v1.1.0 was driven by Claude Code (claude-opus-4-8) on Spec Kit 0.10.2 with Superpowers 6.0.0 live; the v1.2.0 hook-dispatch change and 7-test smoke suite touched no agent-facing protocol.

notes: v1.2.0 adds plug-and-play before_implement/after_implement extension-hook dispatch to the execute command and both per-agent SKILL peers (instruction-only, mirroring Spec Kit's own implement command) so the bridge is a true drop-in for speckit.implement; the dispatch skips the bridge's own before_implement guard hook. No new command, hook, script, state file, or schema; guard rules, handoff v1 schema, command count (3), hook count (5), actor semantics, and the >=0.8.10 runtime floor are unchanged. The v1.1.0 Superpowers 6.0.0 alignment and the 2026-06-18 Spec Kit 0.11.1 maintenance pass remain valid baselines. Dated Windows PowerShell and agent rows from v1.0.0 are retained because the corresponding bytes did not change.
